newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordanian shares continue weak trend.
newsitem.headline: Jordanian shares continue weak trend.

text.p: Jordanian stocks closed 0.24 percent lower on Monday for the third consecutive day in dull trading as investors remained on the sidelines, brokers said.

"The market was slightly better than on Sunday but nothing special...with the only activity on solid companies expected to announce good earnings," said Nasser al-Amad, head of United Financial Investments.

The official Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.38 points to 155.73 points in turnover of 562,373 dinars ($794,312) with nearly a third dominated by a bloc sale in Jordan National Bank worth 150,053 dinars.
Brokers said depressed investor sentiment continued to depress the market with renewed selling pressure surfacing again in the absence of any new factors to reactivate declining turnover this month.

Investor sentiment has recently soured over worries about the fate of $120 million worth of orders won by Jordanian firms under the U.N. "oil-for food" deal because of approval delays along with growing doubts about the government's seriousness in implementing its privatisation pledge.
Continued shareholder activity on Livestock and Poultry buttressed the stock at an unchanged 0.59 dinars in the second largest trade on Monday worth 121,427 dinars.

The two other more heavily traded stocks on Monday posted modest losses: Arab Bank shed 2.50 dinars to 263 dinars and Unified Company dropped 0.01 dinars to 1.79 dinars in low trade worth 20,679 dinars.
Thirteen stocks rose and another 12 rose on Monday, while seventeen traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 most-traded shares on the exchange shed 0.18 percent to 81.54 points, 2.23 percent down from the start of the year.
